report:
mode nodata, snapshot scn not modified but later on error ORA-01555

Hi,
We managed to move to mode "no data" using signal to make blocking snapshot form table to table, (200 big tables, so 1 by 1).
Everything is working fine except today:
- The "snapshot_scn" keeps the same all the time (no change)
- Blocking snapshots (1 by 1 by signal) are ok, putting log mining in pause
- Then log mining replays from previously scn stored
- and so on
But today:
- start of snapshot goes in error with a ORA-01555 error snapshot too old: rollback segment number 127 with name "_SYSSMUXXX_1234567890$" too small
The snapshot scn is too old, which is normal as it is very old (2 weeks).
But as it starts a new fresh snapshot, Debezium should not rely on this value, right?
Should be restart the Debezium with commit_scn, scn and also snapshot_scn in the offset topic ?
Best regards,
Frederic

evidence.quote: When using blocking snapshots, the same requirements around ORA-01555 hold. That's because a blocking snapshot is effectively an on-demand initial snapshot. You need to use incremental snapshots

notes: Blocking snapshot uses a flashback AS OF SCN query that exceeds UNDO retention on a huge table (ORA-01555); reporter first blamed a stale snapshot_scn in Debezium, then accepted the undo explanation.

reviews.fix: Use incremental snapshots instead of blocking snapshots for very large Oracle tables to avoid ORA-01555.
reviews.evidence: Chris Cranford: "You need to use incremental snapshots if you want to avoid ORA-01555 errors when you have very large tables." fredbregier: "Yes, I understand my mistake"
reviews.boundary: B vs C: raising Oracle UNDO_RETENTION would be C, but the adopted fix is changing snapshot usage, so B

reviews.fix: Use incremental snapshots instead of blocking snapshots for very large tables, since blocking snapshots rely on Oracle undo retention and hit ORA-01555 by design.
reviews.evidence: Chris Cranford: "When using blocking snapshots, the same requirements around ORA-01555 hold... You need to use incremental snapshots if you want to avoid ORA-01555 errors when you have very large tables."
